title: Idioms: owls in the bog and cows on the ice
title_target: Ingen ko på isen, Lars. Jag har is i magen.
goal: Understand and use the most common Swedish idioms, inflect them correctly, and avoid the classic learner mistakes of swapping or mixing their fixed parts.
bekal: you can understand about thirty everyday idioms such as *ingen ko på isen*, *ana ugglor i mossen* and *glida in på en räkmacka*
you can put an idiom into the right tense and person without breaking it
you can match Swedish idioms with their English counterparts — and spot where they differ
wave: Go back to Unit 8: idiomatic particle verbs are idioms too. Say *stå ut med*, *ta itu med* and *slå igenom* in a sentence each, and check that the stress falls on the particle.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Söndagsmiddag
dialogs.intro: Sunday dinner at Anna and Lars's. Dian has just had her final interview for a job at a sustainability consultancy in Stockholm — with Kristina, who would be her manager — and Lars wants to hear all about it. Dian has a list of phrases from the interview that she doesn't quite understand.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Nå, Dian, hur gick anställningsintervjun?
lines.id: So, Dian, how did the job interview go?
lines.literal: well, Dian, how went employment-interview-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Bra, tror jag! Fast i slutet sa chefen att ingen på deras kontor har glidit in på en räkmacka. Ska jag bli orolig?
lines.id: Well, I think! Though at the end the manager said nobody at their office had “slid in on a shrimp sandwich”. Should I be worried?
lines.literal: good, believe I! though in end-the said boss-the that nobody at their office has glided in on a shrimp-sandwich. shall I become worried?

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Tvärtom, det låter bra. Hon menar att alla där har slitit för det de har.
lines.id: On the contrary, that sounds good. She means everyone there has worked hard for what they've got.
lines.literal: on-the-contrary, it sounds good. she means that all there have toiled for that they have.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Den som glider in på en räkmacka får allt serverat utan att anstränga sig.
lines.id: Someone who slides in on a shrimp sandwich gets everything handed to them without lifting a finger.
lines.literal: the-one who glides in on a shrimp-sandwich gets everything served without to strain himself.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Men varför just en räkmacka?
lines.id: But why a shrimp sandwich, of all things?
lines.literal: but why exactly a shrimp-sandwich?

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Det vet ingen riktigt. Men räkor har alltid varit lite lyx.
lines.id: Nobody really knows. But shrimp have always been a bit of a luxury.
lines.literal: it knows nobody really. but shrimps have always been little luxury.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ni har så många sådana uttryck. Hon sa också att det inte var någon ko på isen – beskedet kommer om två veckor.
lines.id: You have so many expressions like that. She also said there was “no cow on the ice” — I'll hear in two weeks.
lines.literal: you-all have so many such expressions. she said also that it not was any cow on ice-the — message-the comes in two weeks.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Det betyder att det inte är bråttom. Ingen fara, alltså.
lines.id: That means there's no hurry. No need to worry, in other words.
lines.literal: it means that it not is hurried. no danger, thus.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Men på vägen ut hörde jag en kollega till henne säga att hon anade ugglor i mossen.
lines.id: But on my way out I heard one of her colleagues say she “sensed owls in the bog”.
lines.literal: but on way-the out heard I a colleague to her say that she sensed owls in bog-the.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Då misstänkte hon att något inte stod rätt till. Säkert om något helt annat.
lines.id: Then she suspected something wasn't quite right. About something else entirely, no doubt.
lines.literal: then suspected she that something not stood right to. surely about something wholly other.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Och om du får jobbet ska du inte ta dig vatten över huvudet i början.
lines.id: And if you get the job, don't go biting off more than you can chew at the start.
lines.literal: and if you get job-the shall you not take yourself water over head-the in beginning-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ingen ko på isen, Lars. Jag har is i magen.
lines.id: No need to worry, Lars. I'm keeping my cool.
lines.literal: no cow on ice-the, Lars. I have ice in stomach-the.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: (skrattar) Två uttryck i samma andetag – du slog två flugor i en smäll!
lines.id: (laughing) Two expressions in one breath — you killed two birds with one stone!
lines.literal: (laughs) two expressions in same breath — you struck two flies in one smack!

notes: **Glida in på en räkmacka** — literally “slide in on a shrimp sandwich”: to get something without having worked for it, to have a free ride. It is almost always used in the negative or as criticism: *Han har glidit in på en räkmacka* (he's had it easy). Said by an employer — *ingen här har glidit in på en räkmacka* — it is a compliment to the whole team, and a hint about what they expect.

**Slita** — literally “to wear out, to tear”, here “to toil, to work very hard”: *Hon har slitit för det hon har*. The same verb gives *sliten* (“worn out”) and *slit och släp* (“toil and drudgery”). It is a strong verb: *slita – slet – slitit*.

**Ingen ko på isen** — literally “no cow on the ice”: there's no hurry, no danger. The full version is *Det är ingen ko på isen så länge rumpan är på land* — “there's no cow on the ice as long as its backside is on land”, i.e. no problem as long as things are still under control. The negation is built in: you never say *det är en ko på isen*.

**Ana ugglor i mossen** — literally “sense owls in the bog”: to smell a rat, to suspect something is wrong. *Ana* (**AH-nah**) means “to sense, to have a hunch”, and appears in *Jag anade det!* (“I had a feeling!”). *Inte stå rätt till* is the neutral way to say “not be right”.

**Ta sig vatten över huvudet** — literally “take water over one's head”: to take on more than you can handle. It is reflexive, so the pronoun changes with the person: *Jag tog mig vatten över huvudet*, *Ta dig inte vatten över huvudet!* Notice that the unstressed *dig* comes **before** *inte* in the imperative.

**Ha is i magen** — “have ice in the stomach”: to stay calm under pressure. English keeps its cool in the head, Swedish in the stomach. **Slå två flugor i en smäll** — “swat two flies in one smack” — is the Swedish “kill two birds with one stone”: kinder to birds, harder on flies.

grammars.title: Idioms are grammar too
body: An idiom is a fixed phrase, but it is not frozen: its verb still changes for tense, its reflexive pronoun still follows the subject, and its negation still obeys word-order rules. What you must never change are the **nouns and numbers** at its core.

head: Idiom (base form)
What changes
Example
rows: Jag **har anat** ugglor i mossen länge.
Då **slog** du två flugor i en smäll.
Filmen var inte **spännande** för fem öre.

after: **Never swap the fixed words.** *Inte rolig för fem kronor* is wrong even though *öre* coins disappeared in 2010 — the idiom keeps the old coin. *Tre flugor i en smäll* or *en uggla i mossen* will make Swedes smile, and not with you.
**Some idioms are negative by nature.** *Ingen ko på isen*, *inte för fem öre*, *det är inte hela världen* only exist in the negative; *inte ugglor i mossen* doesn't exist at all.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Femton nya idiom
dialogs.intro: That evening Dian calls Oskar in Göteborg. She has collected fifteen idioms over the weekend and is keen to try them out. Not all of them survive the journey.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Oskar! Jag har lärt mig femton nya idiom i helgen.
lines.id: Oskar! I've learned fifteen new idioms this weekend.
lines.literal: Oskar! I have learned myself fifteen new idioms in weekend-the.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Oj. Låt höra.
lines.id: Whoa. Let's hear them.
lines.literal: oh. let hear.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jobbsökandet går som tåget, men chefen på intervjun var inte rolig för fem kronor.
lines.id: The job hunt is going great, but the manager at the interview wasn't funny “for five kronor”.
lines.literal: job-searching-the goes like train-the, but boss-the at interview-the was not funny for five kronor.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: För fem öre, inte fem kronor! Och säg inte det högt om du börjar där.
lines.id: For five öre, not five kronor! And don't say that out loud if you start there.
lines.literal: for five öre, not five kronor! and say not that loud if you start there.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Okej. Och hennes kollega? Hon sa att där låg en hund i mossen.
lines.id: OK. And her colleague? She said there was “a dog in the bog”.
lines.literal: okay. and her colleague? she said that there lay a dog in bog-the.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Nu blandar du ihop två uttryck. Det heter ”där ligger en hund begraven”. Och hon sa nog ugglor i mossen.
lines.id: Now you're mixing up two expressions. It's “there lies a dog buried”. And she probably said owls in the bog.
lines.literal: now mix you together two expressions. it is-called “there lies a dog buried”. and she said probably owls in bog-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jaha. Och om jag köper något utan att titta på det först?
lines.id: I see. And if I buy something without looking at it first?
lines.literal: I-see. and if I buy something without to look at it first?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Då köper du grisen i säcken. Det har alla gjort någon gång.
lines.id: Then you're buying a pig in a poke. Everybody's done that at some point.
lines.literal: then buy you pig-the in sack-the. that have all done some time.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Som när jag hyrde rummet i Majorna utan att ha sett det.
lines.id: Like when I rented the room in Majorna without having seen it.
lines.literal: like when I rented room-the in Majorna without to have seen it.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Precis. Men ärligt talat – du är inte ute och cyklar. Du låter nästan som en infödd.
lines.id: Exactly. But honestly — you're not way off. You almost sound like a native.
lines.literal: exactly. but honestly spoken — you are not out and cycle. you sound almost like a native-born.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Nästan? Då har jag en bit kvar.
lines.id: Almost? Then I still have a way to go.
lines.literal: almost? then have I a bit left.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Det är inte hela världen. Det är lugnt.
lines.id: It's not the end of the world. It's all good.
lines.literal: it is not whole world-the. it is calm.

notes: **Går som tåget** — “goes like the train”: things are going really well. Swedish trains are not famous for punctuality, which makes the idiom slightly ironic today, but nobody hears it that way.

**Inte rolig för fem öre** — “not funny in the least”. *Öre* (**Ö-reh**) is a hundredth of a krona; the coins vanished in 2010, but the idiom kept them. Change *öre* to *kronor* and the joke is on you. Oskar's warning is the other lesson: saying it about a future boss, anywhere near the office, would be a serious misjudgment.

**Där ligger en hund begraven** — “there lies a dog buried”: there's something fishy, that's the real issue. German has exactly the same idiom (*Da liegt der Hund begraben*). Dian has crossed it with *ugglor i mossen* — mixing two idioms is called *att blanda ihop uttryck*, and Swedes find it charming, at least once.

**Köpa grisen i säcken** — “buy the pig in the sack”, which is English “buy a pig in a poke” (a *poke* is an old word for a bag). This is one of the many idioms Swedish and English share from medieval market life.

**Vara ute och cykla** — “be out cycling”: to be completely wrong, to have no idea what you're talking about. *Du är ute och cyklar!* is a frank but friendly way to tell someone they're wrong. Oskar uses it in the negative as praise.

**Det är lugnt** — “it's fine, no worries”, from *lugn* (“calm”). It is one of the most frequent phrases in spoken Swedish: an answer to *förlåt*, to *tack*, and to “sorry I'm late”. Together with *ingen fara* and *det är inte hela världen*, it is how Swedes tell each other not to worry.

grammars.title: Swedish idioms and their English cousins
body: Some idioms translate word for word, some swap the image, and some have no English counterpart at all.

head: Swedish
Literally
English equivalent
rows: slide in on a shrimp sandwich
bite off more than one can chew
slå två flugor i en smäll
swat two flies in one smack
kill two birds with one stone
buy the pig in the sack
buy a pig in a poke

after: Watch the last row: Swedes **hold their thumbs** (*Jag håller tummarna för dig!*), physically tucking them inside their fists. Crossing your fingers means nothing in particular in Sweden.

Don't translate English idioms into Swedish word for word. *Det regnar katter och hundar* is not Swedish; Swedes say *Det regnar småspik* (“it's raining little nails”) or *Det öser ner* (“it's pouring”).

blocks.text: Idioms are easier to remember in groups. Swedish draws heavily on farm animals, food and the body — the world of a country that was rural until the twentieth century.

head: Family
Idiom
Meaning
rows: be sly (have a fox behind the ear)
gå åt som smör i solsken
sell like hot cakes (go like butter in sunshine)
that's not my responsibility (not my table)
poke one's nose in (put one's nose in the soak)
it's not the end of the world

blocks.title: Workplace favorites
items: *Det är inte mitt bord* — very common in offices, and slightly passive-aggressive: “not my department”.
*Vi får ta det som det kommer* — “we'll take it as it comes”.
*Nu ska vi inte gå över ån efter vatten* — “let's not cross the river to fetch water”: don't make things more complicated than necessary.
*Det är bara att gilla läget* — “just accept the situation”, literally “like the position”.

blocks.text: Idioms are where learners sound most charming and most foreign at the same time. One well-placed idiom per conversation is a pleasure for your listener; five in a row, as Dian found out, is a performance.

items: **Learn the whole phrase**, including the little words: *ana ugglor **i** mossen*, *glida in **på** en räkmacka*, *slå två flugor **i** en smäll*.
**Check the polarity**: is the idiom positive (*gå som tåget*), negative (*ingen ko på isen*) or both?
**Check the register**: *det är lugnt* fits anywhere; *vara ute och cykla* is frank; *inte rolig för fem öre* about a person is rude.
**Start with the safe five**: *det är lugnt*, *ingen fara*, *det är inte hela världen*, *hålla tummarna*, *gå som tåget*.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 13
items: Unit 13 ended with an idiom: *tåget har gått* (“the ship has sailed”).
Combine idioms with wishes and regrets: *Hade jag bara anat ugglor i mossen!* · *Jag önskar att jag inte hade köpt grisen i säcken.* · *Du borde inte ha tagit dig vatten över huvudet.*
Notice that the idiom's verb takes whatever form the grammar asks for — *anat*, *köpt*, *tagit* — while the nouns stay fixed.

exercises.title: Translate
exercises.prompt: Translate into Swedish, using an idiom where possible.
items: Keep your cool!
It's not the end of the world.
I'll keep my fingers crossed for you.
Don't worry, there's no rush.
